comments.author: @torarinvik4920
comments.text:
I seriously hope that someone tries to make a language based OS, sort of similar to Andrei Karpathy's vision. This is my idea: You have an OS similar to a virtual machine, this VM is a neuro-symbolic AI. The AI takes queries or tasks in the form of natural language, it synthesizes programs to solve the task built up by composing new programs based on existing ones. The programs gets assembled to CPU and GPU instructions and is run on the OS/VM. The AI can reflect on the output by reading the output from the executed assembled instructions.

The challenge with neuro-symbolic AI is that neural nets work with continuous data eg. probabilities and streams. Symbolic AI works with discreet data in the form of a single precise output. The effective integration of these two paradigms at scale remains an open challenge, which is partly why pure neural approaches like LLMs currently dominate. The potential benefit of neuro-symbolic AI is that it can generalize better and learn few-shot, it needs a lot less data to learn and can potentially be more precise in specific domains. Rather than having a neural net output probabilistic distributions, it produces structured programs that can be directly executed on hardware, creating a more transparent and verifiable system.
